---
title: "1. Introduction"
subtitle: "What is a Pico, and why build one?"
---

## Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you will be able to:

- Describe what a Pico is in one sentence.
- Name the three main components (Rules, Parser, Composer) and their role.
- Identify where a Pico sits in the Open Engineering ecosystem.

## Prerequisites

- A working shell and text editor.
- Comfort reading YAML.
- No prior Pico experience is required.

## What is a Pico?

A **Pico** is the smallest useful Open Engineering artifact: a declarative,
composable unit described by **Rules** and produced by a **Parser** and a
**Composer**. See the [Glossary](../../glossary.qmd) for full definitions of
each term.

::: {.callout-tip}
If you can describe a thing with a handful of Rules and produce it from
those Rules, you can model it as a Pico.
:::

## The Rules → Parser → Composer pipeline

```
Rules  ─────▶  Parser  ─────▶  Composer  ─────▶  Pico
(YAML)         (reads Rules)   (produces output)  (hello-world-pico)
```

Part 2 walks through this pipeline in detail. This lesson focuses on
vocabulary and the mental model.
